title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.28
exact_target: Ask how large the asymptotic-value set of a finite-order meromorphic function can be. The source reports examples of positive and zero order with the entire Riemann sphere as that set. \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200}{[S2]}
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Shared notation.}$\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$, and $\mathbb Z,\mathbb Q,\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ denote the integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers. Any other conventions are specified locally.


For a nonconstant meromorphic function $f$ on $\mathbb C$, let $n(r,a,f)$ count the solutions of $f(z)=a$ in $|z|\le r$, with multiplicity; $a=\infty$ counts poles. Let $\bar n$ count each point once. The integrated count is
\[
 N(r,a,f)=n(0,a,f)\log r+\sum_{0<|z|\le r,\ f(z)=a}\log(r/|z|),
\]
where the sum repeats each point according to multiplicity; $\bar N$ has the same formula without repetitions. Write $\log^+x=\max(\log x,0)$ and
\[
 m(r,\infty,f)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log^+|f(re^{it})|\,dt,\quad
 m(r,a,f)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log^+\frac1{|f(re^{it})-a|}\,dt\quad(a\in\mathbb C).
\]
The Nevanlinna characteristic is $T(r,f)=m(r,\infty,f)+N(r,\infty,f)$. Its order and lower order are
\[
 \rho(f)=\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log T(r,f)}{\log r},\qquad
 \lambda(f)=\liminf_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log T(r,f)}{\log r}.
\]
The deficiency is $\delta(a,f)=1-\limsup_{r\to\infty}N(r,a,f)/T(r,f)$, and the reduced-count index is $\Theta(a,f)=1-\limsup_{r\to\infty}\bar N(r,a,f)/T(r,f)$. A value is deficient if $\delta(a,f)>0$. An entire function is holomorphic on all of $\mathbb C$; for an entire function, $M(r,f)=\max_{|z|=r}|f(z)|$.

A path to infinity is a continuous curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ with $|\gamma(t)|\to\infty$. A value $a\in\widehat{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ is an asymptotic value of $f$ if $f(\gamma(t))\to a$ along such a path, using the spherical topology when $a=\infty$.
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For finite-order meromorphic functions $f$, determine universal upper restrictions, if any, on
\[
 \mathcal A(f)=\{a\in\widehat{\mathbb C}:a\text{ is an asymptotic value of }f\}.
\]
In particular, can this set be all of $\widehat{\mathbb C}$ even when $\rho(f)<\infty$? The question concerns meromorphic functions and all asymptotic values, rather than only direct singularities of an inverse function. \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200}{[S2]}

\subsection{Short English statement}
Ask how large the asymptotic-value set of a finite-order meromorphic function can be. The source reports examples of positive and zero order with the entire Riemann sphere as that set. \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07200}{[S2]}
